title: Yet, Heard
essence: Three calls made at the edge of a harbour before leaving: to the lover under a shared moon, to the mother over a black hole that opens in the water, to the father who walks out of the eastern sky. One night on one quay, and the light is the clock: moon high, the dead hour, first grey, the sun coming up out of the harbour mouth. Each call is a dashed line of light strung between two people, and behind every call the same breakup keeps playing on the sidewalk.
palette_notes: Night navy and harbour teal from the bay stills (3238a164 lamps on black water, ef9f6c7e night quay); sodium amber of the quay lamps and the town across the water from the same two; neon red only in the club sidewalk opening (b05d5b9a puddle, 7fdacba9 street); the moon is paper cream, never pure white. Dawn walks the sky from slate grey (#8a8f9a) to sunrise apricot (#f2b35a) in M3-M4. Electric blue (#2f6bff) is the poem's single accent: 'someone blue', one point of light on the poet's chest in the last few seconds, nowhere else.

full_text.line: Accepting you'll never say nor ever feel, my love was real.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
I gather my things to go.
Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it
and settle down the stillnessism.
We talk for years and travel through time
and it feels so good.
We grow old together.
I believe maybe we could have it all,
or swing in my humbled late nights and heartbreaks
and an end story unchanging.
You help me gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my mother.
In tears, speaking of an abyss, she's never known.
And we talk for years and we closet wounds
and we explain my way of birth then and even after prayer.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
We grow old together with the moon looking at us
the way we used to be.
As my tears fall between the creases and faith,
dancing on my own, maternal ears in tune.
She watches us gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my father.
Summon his calming demeanor from the yonders
and we walk for years and travel east toward the sunrises
and retrace his footsteps now and then.
Guiding a settling down moon the way it used to leave
and my tears fall between the creases
and wave shadows of the inner harbor.
We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken.
Someone borrowed and someone blew.
Yet broken, yet hurt.

arc.beat: out of the club, through a fawning crowd, he glimpses EX's back and cannot reach him; then the two of them walk the waterfront and look up at the same moon while the years pass as moonlight
arc.image: two backs on the quay lip, heads tipped up at one paper moon, each with his own road of light on the water opening into a V

arc.beat: suitcases on the sidewalk; he calls his mother from a lit booth while the breakup plays behind him; she weeps and the harbour between them goes bottomless
arc.image: the call-cord sagging into a black hole cut in the water, tears peeling off the cord and falling into nothing

arc.beat: he hangs up, the mother dissolves; he dials again and the father resolves out of the paling east; they walk the quay east, the son stepping into prints already worn in the stone
arc.image: a dark footprint trail on wet stone pointing east under the first grey

arc.beat: father and son stroll into the sunrise, one brief shake on 'shaken'; back at the booth EX turns to haze and is gone; the poet stands alone in first sun
arc.image: a half sun sitting in the harbour mouth, harbour lights going out, one blue point on the poet's chest

insights: Build one harbour and relight it four times rather than four sets: the light is the clock (moon, dead hour, grey, sunrise).
The cord is the call. Keep it dashed and pulsing; it is the cheapest way to say 'on the phone' across a wide frame.
The breakup must keep playing in the background of every call: use a second, smaller POET + EX pair on a far layer, looped.
Dissolves are rationed: only the mother leaving, the father arriving and EX's haze. Every other change is a cut.
Aging must never be literal: years pass as the moon climbing.
Hold the blue accent back to the final seconds; it is the only time blue appears in the poem.

Atlas: the Halfworld frames (foundry/09-02, 09-03) already solve the poem in cut-out terms: two flat silhouettes, one paper moon, a dashed arc between heads. Match their flatness; don't let the call become a glowing tube.
Atlas: in the Arcade all colour belongs to light (neon strips, reflections, the booth's white); paint the walls nearly black so the coded light reads.
Atlas: the 09-to-10 cut is physical: booth and bike share one lamp on one curb. Park the bike card in the dark of 09.5 so 10 starts without a cut.
future: Harbour quay kit and the moon/sun discs return in 13 (the harbour) and the sunrise light feeds 11.
Elder FATHER walk cycle can be reused for the remembered elders in 12.
The dot-dissolve card technique carries to the ghost child and to 10's dawn sweep.
The poet's suitcase leaves with him; the empty sidewalk where 10 starts is this sidewalk at the end of the night.

atlas.district_language: Two districts, one night. The Shrouded Arcade (03:30, rain) is the club sidewalk and the booth curb: paint the facades flat and dark (#272225 / #394b5a), and let ALL colour come from coded light: pink-magenta neon (#be5791) and red-blue signs as glowing strips cut into the cards, doubled underneath as wobbling reflection strips on a glossy black floor card. The booth is the only white light, a cold rectangle that spills a trapezoid onto the curb. The LED canopy is a sky card of moving colour held high, never lower than the +4 m line; we see its underside only, never its ends. Mirror Thread Bay (the inner harbour, pre-dawn) is water first: frame low, reflections before subjects; the quay is a dark stone strip, the water a black glossy card with lamp-columns of teal and sodium orange broken into dashes. The light is the clock: neon and moon, then the dead hour, then the orange haze of first light (views/085, 080) where everything flattens to two values. Never show: daylight crowds, the canopy's structure, the EX's face, any colour in the mother's room that isn't lamp-warm.

best.element: two black silhouettes on a dotted grey ground, a dashed arc of light bowing between their heads, a white moon above
best.why: this IS the call-cord: a dashed line strung head to head, bowed up like a skipping rope. Copy its dash rhythm (long dash, short gap) and its sag.

best.element: the same two silhouettes walking side by side, paper moon half-sunk behind a cloud band
best.why: 09.1 in pure cut-out grammar: two flat backs, one moon, everything else halftone. The animator's key for the walk toward the moon.

best.element: rain-soaked street, neon doubled in the asphalt, power lines, a lit sign at the curb
best.why: the booth curb itself: flat dark verticals, colour only in the reflections. Build the floor as a glossy card with painted reflection strips.

best.element: a red booth against a bare grey wall, two coated men from behind, four leather cases on the pavement
best.why: the suitcase beat composed as a frieze: booth centre, two backs, cases at their heels. Re-dress at night and in our booth colours; keep the flat side-on layout.

best.element: a neon corridor reflected in one long puddle running to the vanishing point
best.why: the puddle insert of 09.1: one mirror card the length of the street, red walls, blue path.

best.element: a pier walkway with an orange light strip along each kerb, two small figures walking away into haze
best.why: father and son walking east (09.4): two backs, two glowing lines converging, the whole frame one orange.

best.element: a canal under a bridge at night, teal and sodium lamps doubled as long broken columns on black water
best.why: the inner harbour before dawn: exactly how to paint lamp reflections as stacked dashes on the water card.

best.element: a lone figure walking a wet road toward a low pink sun through haze
best.why: the father's road east at first grey: one figure, one sun, bokeh blots; a two-value pink plate.

best.element: a crowd in motion blur, backs and shoulders, pink and gold light
best.why: the fawning crowd outside the club (09.0): heads and shoulders as one smeared strip, the EX lost among them.

best.element: a small living room: net-curtained window, side shelves, a chair, framed prints
best.why: mother's room as a modest real place; the big bright window is where the sidewalk breakup is held.

best.element: an LED vault of swirling colour over an avenue with palms and a dense crowd
best.why: the Shrouded Arcade's canopy: a high sky card of moving colour over the club street (hero).

staging.name: The EX in the crowd
staging.shot: handheld-feel follow on the street plane: three crowd strips at different depths slide past the lens (foreground strip blurred, oversized); the EX is a back in the mid strip under a pink door glow; POET's hand card reaches in from frame-left foreground and is blocked by a shoulder card. Neon signs pulse on the back plate.

staging.name: Walking toward the moon
staging.shot: long lens from behind: POET and EX as two back cards side by side centre-low, the street's two kerb lines converging on a paper moon at the vanishing point; the walk is a slow push in, the moon held still. Insert: the puddle card with both inverted reflections wobbling.

staging.name: Suitcases at the phone booth
staging.shot: camera at suitcase height on the curb: the two cases fill the foreground, the booth's white light lays a trapezoid on the wet curb card, POET's legs and the EX's hands and back only enter above the cases. Rain as two layers of short white strokes.

staging.name: The call to Mother
staging.shot: from outside the booth through its glass card (one smear, one reflection strip): POET in the white box with the handset; behind him, on the street plate, the breakup plays as small back cards. Cut to mother's room: armchair, lamp, corded phone; her window card holds the same sidewalk plate. On hang-up she is pulled off on a replacement fade.

staging.name: Father and son to the inner harbor
staging.shot: wide from behind on the quay path: two backs walking away along a kerb light strip toward a pale band of dawn; water card on the right with lamp-dash reflections; the breakup kept small on a far back plate at frame left. Sky band swaps from navy to orange haze in hard steps.

staging.name: The EX turns to haze
staging.shot: locked-off wide two-shot at the booth curb, frontal and flat: POET and the EX's back stand apart; the EX card is replaced in three steps by an orange haze card of his silhouette, then by nothing. Hold on POET alone under the one lamp, the bike's shape already at the kerb in the dark (10).

heroes.name: The LED Canopy and the booth curb
heroes.in_poem: the canopy is the ceiling over the club door in 09.0 and the glow behind the walk in 09.1; at its far end, under one lamp, the booth curb where the cases stand, the calls are made and the EX dissolves (and where the bike waits for 10).
heroes.build_as_cards: Canopy: one long curved sky card hung above the frame top, painted underside only, with a coded scrolling colour texture (magenta/teal/violet) and two rows of palms as silhouette cards beneath it; shopfront cards left and right with cut neon strips. Booth curb: kerb strip, one lamp-post card with a cone of light, the booth as a 3-face fold-out (front glass with folding door that opens, side glass, back panel with the steel phone), lit ceiling panel on a separate glow layer. Nothing breaks: only the light changes.

world_details.detail: the flood line: a pale salt band at 4 m on every old quay and warehouse wall, chalked fresh where a wall is new; the LED canopy is hung above it, never crossing it
world_details.where: quay walls and the club facades

world_details.detail: a Tide Office notice board at the head of the quay ladder: two chalked times and two heights for the next gates
the hot minute: when the gates rise, every harbour lamp brightens together for a beat, then settles; we put it on the line 'travel east' as one synchronised flare of all lamp cards
the city greeting 'where do you go?' / 'when I leave' as a scrawl on the booth's back panel among numbers
the pulse: a cyan ring crossing the facades; the crowd outside the club stops talking while it passes
the chrome door at the end of the alley, red-lit and always shut, glimpsed once behind the crowd (it opens only in 14)
world_details.where: back plate of the club sidewalk

transitions.how: the club's street door opens under the canopy: the door card slides aside and we are on the avenue among the fawning crowd (views/099 to 100).
dissolve on the same curb: the booth and the bike share one lamp. The EX's haze card fades, the lamp stays put, and the bike card (already parked in the dark of 09.5) is lit up by the same cone.
